comparisons.finding: For the same visibly read Slot supplies, trace A deploys the bridge before alignment and walks back to align it; trace B aligns first and then deploys against the retained lock. This is an observed change in operation order, not a name-only difference.

A and C start with Control Bay to Lift Station; B starts with Control Bay to Transfer Table. A's detent preparation revisits Transfer Table and then Service Gallery. B instead restores service first and later returns through Transfer Table to reach the lift. C reaches home after only Lift Station and Return Platform.

The Crescent reports and corresponding visible rows in A/B lead to index one with Blue-only testing. C's actually reported Kite row changes the decision to index two, White-only testing and Amber + White running; B runs on Amber + Blue.

comparisons.dimension: Optional work does not select the rescue approach
comparisons.finding: A successfully tests the lift then crosses the maintenance bridge; B reports both service preparations complete then rides the lift. Passing UI cases assert completed Lift survey and Service restoration milestones respectively. C completes the lift survey as part of its direct-lift route.

exactConfirmationBoundary.traceObservation: Every completed physical action is preceded by a proposal and a separate confirmed event. Each trace includes one additional initial proposal that was deliberately declined by the test; it has no corresponding confirmed event.
exactConfirmationBoundary.limitation: These compact traces do not contain proposal UUIDs or the home card text. Exact commit-id uniqueness and final home/approach assertions are supported by the passing browser cases, not invented from missing trace fields.

boundaries: Different test panel labels and public codes identify three selected cases. The original compact traces do not serialize panel piece geometry, initial/applied rotations or rotation counts. This comparison therefore makes no independent geometric-diversity or rotation-efficiency claim; the separate panel validation and visual evidence cover those questions.
The third run did not inspect service equipment; its test title must not be mistaken for an observed service-procedure report.
Apply counts include only successful acknowledged changes logged by the helper; they are not a claimed optimal number of electrical edits.
These are automated local deterministic Practice runs, not a human playtest, enjoyment/retention result, microphone test, Live Voice result, provider ACK or hosted acceptance.
